title: Theory fails if a complex organ could not arise by slight steps

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Theory fails if a complex organ could not arise by slight steps

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: If any complex organ were shown to exist that could not possibly have been formed by numerous, successive, slight modifications, the theory of natural selection would break down; no such case is known.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If it could be demonstrated that any complex organ existed, which could not possibly have been formed by numerous, successive, slight modifications, my theory would absolutely break down.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Organs of extreme perfection.”. Scope: complex organs of all organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.36

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing data permit case studies but not an exhaustive test over all complex organs. The word 'possibly' also makes decisive discrimination unusually difficult.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For sampled complex organs, reconstruct ancestral states and test whether each transition can be decomposed into small heritable functional changes. One rigorously established organ requiring an inaccessible discontinuity would refute the universal claim, while finite surveys cannot confirm it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Possibility of a pathway is difficult to establish or exclude.

The universal quantifier cannot be confirmed by sampling.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.25
data adequacy: 0.22
operationalizability: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The empirical clause that no such organ is known reports a state of argument rather than a measurable frequency. Any organ still lacking a known intermediate is compatible with the rule, because the rule demands a demonstration of impossibility, which comparative and fossil data cannot supply. Scores stay near the floor because there is no decision criterion a dataset could meet.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The sentence is a falsification rule: the theory fails if some complex organ could not possibly have been reached by successive slight modifications. No measurement records impossibility of every pathway, and a gap in known intermediates does not decide it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Missing intermediates are predicted both by true saltation and by an incomplete record, so the outcomes do not discriminate.

Impossibility of every gradual pathway is modal, not a dataset variable.
